What does zone A mean?

Zone A is a high-risk area: land with a 1 percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year, where FEMA has not worked out how high the water from that flood would reach (44 CFR §59.1, §64.3).

Am I required to buy flood insurance?

Federal law requires it only in a high-risk zone (A or V) with a federally regulated or backed mortgage, or federal help to buy or build (42 U.S.C. §4012a). Outside them, a lender may still require it.

What does it cost in zone A, by state?

The premium is based on the flood risk of the building. The reason for any one zone is not in this data.

How do I get covered?

Most policies start 30 days after you buy. Bought while making, increasing, extending or renewing a mortgage, it can start at closing if the insurer is paid within 10 days (30 if the lender, title company or settlement attorney pays). To buy: call the NFIP at (877) 336-2627, go to FloodSmart.gov, or ask any licensed insurance agent. Every NFIP insurer offers the same rates.

What this page cannot tell you

Your premium, private insurers' prices, your exact zone, why prices rise, and claims paid in this exact zone across the country. FEMA's map and an agent's quote answer those for your address.
